mcqs.q: The gingiva is classified as:
mcqs.explain: The gingiva (with the hard palate) is keratinized masticatory mucosa, bound firmly to bone.

mcqs.q: The three parts of the gingiva are:
mcqs.explain: The gingiva consists of free (marginal) gingiva, attached gingiva and the interdental papilla.

mcqs.q: The interdental papilla fills the space between two adjacent teeth and is described as:
opts: Triangular (in oral/vestibular view) and tent-shaped in 3D
mcqs.explain: The interdental papilla is triangular from the oral/vestibular view and tent-shaped in three dimensions, with a central concave col.

mcqs.q: The interdental col is significant because it is:
opts: The only part of the gingiva covered by non-keratinized epithelium
mcqs.explain: The col (concave area below the contact point) is covered by thin non-keratinized epithelium — the only part of the gingiva that is non-keratinized.

mcqs.q: The outer oral epithelium of the gingiva is:
opts: Keratinized (mostly parakeratinized) with long sharp rete ridges
mcqs.explain: The outer oral epithelium is keratinized stratified squamous (about 75% parakeratinized) with long, sharp rete ridges.

mcqs.q: The sulcular and junctional epithelium of the gingiva are:
mcqs.explain: Both the sulcular epithelium (lining the sulcus) and junctional epithelium (attaching to the tooth) are non-keratinized.

mcqs.q: The lamina propria of the gingiva is composed mainly of:
mcqs.explain: The gingival lamina propria contains dense bundles of collagen fibres, giving it firmness; there is no submucosa.

mcqs.q: The gingiva has NO submucosa, so the lamina propria attaches directly to bone, forming a:
mcqs.explain: With no submucosa, the gingival lamina propria attaches directly to the periosteum of the bone — a firm mucoperiosteum (as in the hard palate).

mcqs.q: The hard palate epithelium is:
mcqs.explain: The hard palate, like the gingiva, is keratinized masticatory mucosa with prominent rete ridges.

mcqs.q: Which midline structure is found at the anterior hard palate?
mcqs.explain: The incisive papilla is a midline elevation at the anterior hard palate (over the incisive foramen); transverse palatine rugae radiate from the median raphe.

mcqs.q: The transverse ridges on the anterior hard palate are the:
mcqs.explain: The palatine rugae are transverse ridges of the anterior hard palate, arranged on either side of the median raphe.

mcqs.q: Which zones of the hard palate contain a submucosa (with fat or glands)?
opts: The fatty zone (anterior) and glandular zone (posterior)
mcqs.explain: The anterolateral fatty zone and posterolateral glandular zone of the hard palate contain a submucosa; the raphe and rugae are bound directly to bone (mucoperiosteum).

mcqs.q: The median raphe region of the hard palate is:
opts: Bound directly to bone (mucoperiosteum, no submucosa)
mcqs.explain: Along the median raphe (and the rugae), the mucosa is bound directly to the periosteum (mucoperiosteum), with no submucosa.

mcqs.q: Free (marginal) gingiva forms the soft-tissue wall of the:
mcqs.explain: The free (marginal) gingiva forms one wall of the gingival sulcus, the tooth surface forming the other.

mcqs.q: Approximately what proportion of the gingival oral epithelium is parakeratinized?
mcqs.explain: About 75% of the gingival oral epithelium is parakeratinized (the remainder orthokeratinized).

mcqs.q: Which epithelium directly attaches the gingiva to the tooth surface?
mcqs.explain: The junctional epithelium (non-keratinized) forms the attachment of the gingiva to the tooth surface.

mcqs.q: Compared with lining mucosa, the gingiva's firmness is due to:
opts: Dense collagen in the lamina propria and direct attachment to bone
mcqs.explain: The gingiva is firm because of its dense collagenous lamina propria and its direct (mucoperiosteal) attachment to bone.

mcqs.q: The posterolateral hard palate contains which structures in its submucosa?
mcqs.explain: The posterolateral (glandular) zone of the hard palate contains minor mucous salivary glands in its submucosa.

mcqs.q: Why does the col have clinical importance in periodontal disease?
opts: Its thin non-keratinized epithelium is more vulnerable to plaque/inflammation
It is the most keratinized area
mcqs.explain: Because the col is thin and non-keratinized, it is more susceptible to bacterial plaque and is often where interdental periodontal disease begins.

mcqs.q: Attached gingiva is:
opts: Firm and bound to the underlying periosteum
mcqs.explain: Attached gingiva is firm, resilient and tightly bound to the underlying periosteum (and tooth/bone).

saqs.q: Name the three parts of the gingiva.
saqs.a: Free (marginal) gingiva, attached gingiva, and the interdental papilla.

saqs.q: What is the interdental col and why is it significant?
saqs.a: The concave area below the contact point of the interdental papilla; it is thin non-keratinized epithelium — the only non-keratinized part of the gingiva (and vulnerable to disease).

saqs.q: Describe the gingival epithelial types and their keratinization.
saqs.a: Outer oral epithelium: keratinized (75% parakeratinized), long rete ridges. Sulcular and junctional epithelium: non-keratinized.

saqs.q: Describe the lamina propria and submucosa of the gingiva.
saqs.a: Lamina propria = dense collagen bundles; no submucosa (attaches directly to bone — mucoperiosteum).

saqs.q: List the surface features of the hard palate.
saqs.a: Incisive papilla (anterior midline), palatine rugae (transverse ridges), and the median raphe.

saqs.q: Which zones of the hard palate have a submucosa and what do they contain?
saqs.a: The fatty zone (anterior) and the glandular zone (posterior); the raphe/rugae are bound directly to bone (mucoperiosteum).
